correctness.rationale: KKT strict convexity and nonnegativity show the unique weighted soft threshold for every real p>1. On each active set/sign region, solve for the multiplier explicitly, giving a sign-conjugate rank-one correction J_S with zero output elsewhere. Every nonempty S is realized by a strictly active outside input, and finite continuous piecewise-affine decomposition gives the exact global maximum, including the interior identity. If J_S is contractive, differentiating ||v+t a||p^p for all v in ker w yields necessary equations: unequal weights for p≠2 or three active coordinates violate them. For p=2 use Hilbert metric-projection nonexpansivity; for n=2 equal weights use the (x−y)/2 rank-one contraction; n=1 is clipping. For n=2 outer-product Hölder norm gives exact closed form. Radius rescales. Standalone checker, replayed from the exact package, passes 1240 deterministic numerical tests, as corroboration rather than infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The final claim is the complete quantitative Lipschitz modulus of a specified nonlinear nearest-point map, with explicit weighted planar formula and all-dimensional rigidity. Duchi 2008 gives Euclidean ℓ1-ball projection algorithms; Kobos 2015 and Jamison–Kamińska–Lewicki provide general linear norm-one hyperplane obstructions; Denkowska 2013 and Kamińska–Lewicki 2004 provide general contractive-set/optimal-set theory. Their implications are explicitly limited to parts of the nonlinear proof/qualitative obstruction, and inspected material does not give this exact map’s active-set global modulus or anisotropic two-dimensional constant. The strongest 2004 full text was inaccessible and remains a stated risk. published-finding corpus searches and own two-week ledger review did not locate a matching quantitative theorem; negative search alone is not treated as novelty proof.

value.rationale: The quantitative sensitivity of nearest sparse ℓ1-ball projections is a natural stability invariant in constrained approximation. The theorem gives an exact piecewise-affine global modulus for arbitrary positive weights and every finite dimension and exponent, identifies the sharp nonexpansive regime, and supplies a nontrivial explicit anisotropic two-parameter planar constant, including strict amplification outside the rigid regimes. It distinguishes projections specifically returning nearest points from the broader pre-existing possibility of nonexpansive retractions. The outcome is a complete natural stability classification, not an arbitrary slice or minor numerical improvement.
